input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 (Materials) allocates deliverable IP the wrong way for us: any Materials not expressly designated default to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third parties) hold all right, title and interest in work product created for Bluefly during the Service performance period. The licence back for Type II Materials is irrevocable, worldwide and paid-up but permits only use, execution, reproduction, display, performance and distribution "within Customer's Enterprise only" — no right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense. That falls short of the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business), so it is a material deviation rather than a wording nit. There is also no statement anywhere (Sections 1, 7, 11.6, 14.17, 14.18) that Customer retains ownership of its Content and Customer Components; the only Content provision imposes responsibility without confirming rights. Our redline defaults unspecified Materials to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to cover modification and sublicensing for our business while leaving IBM's ownership of its pre-existing materials and Base Components intact, and adds a Customer Data/Content ownership sentence. Nothing in the Agreement assigns our IP to IBM (the Required Consents definition only supports service delivery) and no joint ownership is created, so no walk-away issue arises.

proposal.summary: Default deliverables to Customer ownership, broaden the licence to IBM-owned embedded materials, and confirm Customer owns its Content and data.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so unspecified Materials should default to Type I (Customer-owned) and the licence to IBM-owned Type II Materials needs to cover modification and sublicensing for our business. We have also added a sentence confirming that our Content and Customer Components remain ours, with IBM taking only the rights it needs to deliver the Services.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials created during the Service performance period will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, distribute copies of, and sublicense (to Customer's Enterprise, Subcontractors and Services Recipients) Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes.

ops.text: e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright) in and to the Content and the Customer Components, including all data provided by or on behalf of Customer or its Services Recipients. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content or the Customer Components, and IBM receives only the limited rights expressly granted herein to access, use and modify them as necessary to provide the Services.
